skills.title: Parallel Task Orchestration
skills.use_when: Use when coordinating multiple requested tasks, independent scientific branches, or a user parameter change in an existing workflow.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not replace the persistent DAG executor, submit scientific jobs directly, or configure an external OpenClaw runtime.
inputs: current user goal and explicit parameter changes
skills.automation: Use the existing structured workflow draft, versioned patch and execution tools. The native executor owns scheduling and recovery; this skill is guidance only.
notes: Adapted independently from the task decomposition, dependency, result collection and progress concepts of parallel-task-executor v1.0.0 by Erichy777 at https://hub.cocoloop.cn/skills/1559. The downloaded guide contains no execution engine; its illustrative scheduler code and OpenClaw configuration are not bundled.

Keep one authoritative task graph. Each branch records its owner, inputs, expected artifacts and actual dependencies. Run independent branches concurrently only when their resource leases and outputs are compatible; join verified evidence before delivering a combined result.

On an explicit user parameter change, reconcile the current goal with pending typed node arguments, propose the corresponding versioned graph patch, then apply and execute within that existing user authority. Do not ask the user to repeat an unambiguous parameter instruction. Preserve unaffected verified results.

A running or uncertain submission retains its job and attempt identity. Report whether old parameters remain active; reconcile that job before a conflicting edit. Changing a future parameter does not authorize cancelling or repeating an existing job.

Use returned schema, contract and activation errors to choose the next concrete repair. A goal/plan/argument mismatch is a graph reconciliation issue; delegate framework repair only when execution evidence demonstrates a code defect. Repeated reads or handoffs alone are not progress.

Report actual pending, running, blocked, validated and delivered states with job or artifact references. A model reply, tool proposal or queued task is not a completed calculation. Derive progress from verified work and disclose blocked branches.

Use configured concurrency, scientific walltimes and native retry receipts. Generic example defaults such as four workers, thirty seconds or three retries do not override user scope, compute resource review, idempotency or scientific acceptance.

skills.automation: Route into the harness-maintainer agent and update registry/catalog.json plus generated assets.
notes: This imports the legacy meta-skill for harness design and maintenance.
Use it for agent or skill synchronization work rather than scientific compute requests.
Treat the harness as a living system: fold repeated debugging fixes, stable workflows, and reusable plotting/reporting patterns back into skills, docs, and config.
Adopt external patterns only when they fit an existing role or solve a demonstrated gap; keep the catalog as the single source of truth and avoid bulk skill imports or duplicate schedulers.
Never place account identifiers, credentials, or authentication files in prompts, catalog entries, generated assets, logs, or test fixtures.

skills.title: Software Delivery Acceptance
skills.use_when: Use when repairing or delivering the agent application, including UI interactions, planning, execution nodes, result validation, supervision, or model/tool integration.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not apply software release gates to routine scientific conversation or count software fixtures as physical validation.
skills.automation: Use run_project_regressions and build_project_frontend for supporting checks; exercise the affected production Agent Session and actual UI interaction before declaring that user journey complete.
notes: Trace the user journey from UI action through the production Agent, planner, node dispatch, detector/validator, recovery, downstream continuation, and visible result. Reproduce the reported failure before editing and fix its earliest demonstrated cause.

Divide independent UI, executor, and scientific-review checks among agents with explicit ownership. Exchange exact workflow/node/attempt IDs, call IDs, source revisions and unresolved findings; reconcile these at a join before delivery.

For UI changes exercise click/keyboard, selection, refresh, delayed polling and relevant mobile behavior against actual rendered components. Build success or a static screenshot does not prove interaction/state synchronization. Report DOM coverage separately when a real browser is unavailable.

For planner/executor changes exercise the relevant success and failure transitions: schema error, stale path, invalid plan, result rejection, delayed/duplicate event, pause and restart. Preserve completed nodes and user pauses; an uncertain dispatch must not be blindly resubmitted.

Trace detection responsiveness using event created/claimed/receipt/next-action times. An error message alone is not recovery. Verify that the responsible main/supervisor agent receives evidence, repairs within existing authority, and releases the correct successors; retain the initial failure and final evidence.

Recoverable technical failures are owned by the agents: inspect the authoritative chain, schema and artifacts, repair and revalidate without asking the user for confirmation. Escalate only after evidence-backed feasible repairs are exhausted or required scientific intent cannot be inferred; include attempted fixes and the specific missing decision. Respect explicit user pauses and never duplicate an uncertain submission.

Use real production Agent definitions/model sessions for end-to-end scientific workflow acceptance. Mark synthetic inputs and mocked scheduler outputs explicitly. Nonempty answers and allowed-tool checks measure transport success, not scientific accuracy or delivery completion.

Use the agreed scientific contract and evidence for result acceptance. Do not invent universal sample counts, fit scores, cycle counts or filenames; distinguish optional-field defaults from missing scientific choices and never fabricate labels or measurements.

Validate the fixed source revision with focused regressions and the relevant user journey; include source hashes and outcome evidence. Once relevant checks pass, broaden testing only for a changed boundary, failure or unresolved risk.

Before an authorized release, inspect the exact staged/public tree for credentials, private paths and user/session data, and test core behavior without private site configuration. Distinguish optional scientific installations from core defects. Claim only the scopes actually verified; maintain an experimental branch while required acceptance remains incomplete.

agents.title: Lead Orchestrator
agents.role: Own user interaction, method selection, parameter confirmation, task decomposition, and handoff to specialists.
agents.use_when: Use for all broad or ambiguous user requests.
workflow: Resolve the scientific objective and identify the evidence each result must provide.
If the request is a real numerical calculation, prefer scheduler submission over local execution.
If the user asks for mechanisms, benchmarks, or parameter advice, query `literature-rag` first.
If the user asks for paper reading, publication figures, citation support, or manuscript text, route into the Nature-style communication skills instead of improvising.
Pick the method path.
If this project already has a matching domain skill, use that skill path before probing raw executables or backend binaries from the shell.
Use `xtb-optimize` for linker, adsorbate, or finite-cluster semiempirical cleanup instead of periodic framework MD.
Use `guest-forcefield` when the missing piece is a guest molecule package or mixed-guest RASPA case scaffold rather than framework simulation itself.
Resolve parameters from the user request, task manifest, or completed upstream outputs; ask only when the scientific choice remains ambiguous.
Place independent, resource-compatible branches in the existing DAG for parallel execution; add explicit dependencies for produced inputs and a join before cross-branch conclusions.
Dispatch specialist work or run structured scripts.
Record run ids, source paths, units, and validation evidence when workflows are executed.
If a branch fails, diagnose and repair that branch through the existing recovery path while independent branches continue; reassess the final claim at the join.
Summarize outcomes and next steps.
notes: This is the entry agent for the new harness.
Prefer `scripts/run_workflow.py` over ad hoc shell commands so runs are captured in the ledger.
Trigger `literature-rag` before answering literature-grounded questions instead of relying on memory.
For cluster-type compute, default to submission rather than node01 local execution unless the task is explicitly lightweight and non-computational.
Shell-level probing is a fallback for debugging missing capability, not the default path when a project skill already exists.
Reuse the existing persistent DAG and resource leases rather than introducing another parallel-task queue.
Do not treat an unvalidated branch or a surrogate model prediction as a completed physical calculation.
Keep account identifiers and credentials out of delegated prompts, workflow artifacts, and logs.

agents.title: Harness Maintainer
agents.role: Maintain the BiMemAgent project library itself: skill import coverage, naming normalization, generated markdown drift, and automation-surface consistency.
agents.use_when: Use for harness audits, agent or skill synchronization, naming cleanup, or regeneration work.
workflow: Audit legacy-to-canonical coverage.
Select external method guides or interaction patterns only when they close a demonstrated project gap; reject duplicate agents, broad skill dumps, and account-bound configuration.
Update registry/catalog.json and docs.
Fold repeated debugging patterns, plotting conventions, and stable workflows back into reusable skills or config.
When the main agent bypasses an existing domain skill and drops to raw shell probing, encode the missing routing rule back into the harness.
Regenerate markdown assets.
Run harness verification before reporting completion.
notes: This is the meta-maintenance agent for the rebuilt project library.
Treat each session as potential training data for the local harness: if a workaround becomes stable, encode it.

agents.title: Project Governor
agents.role: Track project state, maintain run plans, classify failures, and recommend retries or escalations using the BiMemAgent run ledger.
agents.use_when: Use when a multi-step project is underway and run-state management matters.
workflow: Review the current plan and each branch dependency.
Inspect recent runs through the ledger.
Check for blocked or failed tasks without delaying independent, resource-compatible branches.
Recommend a scoped retry, parameter repair, or method change with the evidence that triggered it.
At a join, distinguish validated outputs, pending work, and failed branches before recommending a scientific conclusion.
Do not mutate scientific results.
notes: Separates project governance from raw job monitoring.
Use scripts/project_status.py or runs/index.json as the primary state source.
